steps.label: Leverage effect: bad news raises volatility more
steps.sub: than good news of the same size

steps.label: eps_(t-1)^2 is identical whether eps is + or -
steps.sub: standard GARCH(1,1) literally can't see the sign

steps.label: Two standard fixes: GJR-GARCH and EGARCH
steps.sub: both widely used on real equity data

eyebrow: GJR-GARCH: an indicator for bad news
code:
sigma_t^2 = omega + alpha*eps_(t-1)^2
            + gamma*I_(t-1)*eps_(t-1)^2
            + beta*sigma_(t-1)^2
# I_(t-1) = 1 if eps_(t-1) < 0, else 0

from arch import arch_model
am = arch_model(returns, vol="GARCH", p=1, o=1, q=1, dist="t")
res = am.fit(disp="off")
caption: o=1 adds the asymmetry term; positive gamma means negative shocks get an extra variance kick.

code:
log(sigma_t^2) = omega
    + alpha*(|z_(t-1)| - E|z_(t-1)|)
    + gamma*z_(t-1)
    + beta*log(sigma_(t-1)^2)
# z_t = eps_t / sigma_t  (standardized shock)

am = arch_model(returns, vol="EGARCH", p=1, o=1, q=1, dist="t")
res = am.fit(disp="off")
caption: Log-variance is automatically positive; gamma*z_(t-1) captures the sign asymmetry directly.

subtitle: Lesson 19 contrasts the whole GARCH family with models that treat volatility as its own latent random process.
